history.heading: Lan Xang
paragraphs: Laos, the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, lies along the Mekong River. The mysterious Plain of Jars, with thousands of ancient stone jars, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Tai-speaking peoples migrated into the region from southern China.

In 1353 Fa Ngum founded the Kingdom of Lan Xang ("Land of a Million Elephants"), which made Theravada Buddhism the state religion and became a major power. In 1707 it split into three kingdoms, Luang Prabang, Vientiane and Champasak, which later fell under Siamese domination.

history.heading: French Indochina and war
paragraphs: France took control of Laos in 1893 and made it part of French Indochina. Laos became independent in 1953, but civil war followed between the royal government and the communist Pathet Lao, linked to the Vietnam War.

During the Vietnam War, the United States conducted a secret bombing campaign, dropping more than two million tons of bombs between 1964 and 1973, making Laos the most heavily bombed country per person in history. Unexploded bombs still kill and injure people today. In 1975 the Pathet Lao took power, abolished the monarchy and established the Lao People's Democratic Republic.

culture.heading: Buddhist traditions
paragraphs: Lao is the official language. Most ethnic Lao are Theravada Buddhists, and monks' morning alms rounds in Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage town, are a famous sight. Many ethnic minorities, such as the Hmong and Khmu, follow animist beliefs.

The Lao New Year (Pi Mai) in April is celebrated with water festivities. Sticky rice is the staple, eaten with dishes such as larb (minced meat salad) and tam mak hoong (papaya salad). Music features the khaen, a bamboo mouth organ recognised by UNESCO.

politics.heading: Communist state
paragraphs: Laos is a one-party socialist state governed by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party. The National Assembly is elected, but only party-approved candidates can run. Political opposition and independent media are not permitted. Laos maintains close relations with Vietnam and China and is a member of ASEAN.

economy.heading: Battery of Asia
paragraphs: Laos has built many hydropower dams on the Mekong and its tributaries, exporting electricity to neighbouring countries, earning it the nickname "battery of Southeast Asia". Mining (copper and gold), agriculture and tourism are also important. The China–Laos railway, opened in 2021, connects Vientiane to China.
Heavy borrowing, much of it from China, has led to a debt crisis, high inflation and a sharp fall in the value of the kip, the national currency.
